items.followUp: Why is the third ionization energy of magnesium greater than its second ionization energy?

rubric.why: After the first ionization, the second electron is removed from the positively charged Mg⁺ ion.
rubric.description: Identifies the ion from which the second electron is removed.
rubric.how: Look for the second electron being removed from Mg⁺ or a positive ion.

rubric.why: The remaining electrons are attracted more strongly to the nucleus, so more energy is needed to remove the second electron.
rubric.description: Explains why the second ionization energy is higher.
rubric.how: Look for stronger attraction to the nucleus or the need for more energy.

modelAnswer: Magnesium has the electronic configuration 2,8,2; after losing its first electron, it forms Mg⁺.
The second electron is removed from this positive ion.
The remaining electrons are attracted more strongly to the nucleus, so more energy is required to remove the second electron than the first.

items.followUp: Give four differences between an element and a compound.

rubric.why: A compound has a definite composition, whereas a mixture can have variable composition; their components are chemically combined and physically mixed, respectively.
rubric.description: Compares composition and how the substances are joined.
rubric.how: Award for both a fixed-versus-variable composition comparison and a chemical-versus-physical combination comparison.

rubric.why: A compound has properties different from those of its constituent elements and is separated chemically; mixture components retain their properties and can be separated physically.
rubric.description: Compares properties and methods of separation.
rubric.how: Award for both a properties comparison and a chemical-versus-physical separation comparison.

rubric.why: A compound has a definite formula, whereas a mixture has no fixed formula.
rubric.description: Compares the formula of a compound and a mixture.
rubric.how: Look for a definite formula contrasted with no fixed formula.

modelAnswer: A compound has a fixed composition; a mixture has a variable composition.
The elements in a compound are chemically combined; the substances in a mixture are physically mixed.
A compound has properties different from those of its constituent elements; the components of a mixture retain their properties.
A compound can be separated into its elements by chemical methods; a mixture can be separated by physical methods.
A compound has a definite chemical formula; a mixture has no fixed chemical formula.

items.followUp: Define hydrogen bonding and describe two effects it has on the physical properties of water.

rubric.why: Hydrogen bonding is an intermolecular attraction involving hydrogen covalently bonded to F, O, or N and an electronegative atom in a neighbouring molecule.
rubric.description: Defines hydrogen bonding and identifies the atoms and molecules involved.
rubric.how: Look for an intermolecular attraction, covalently bonded hydrogen, and an atom in a neighbouring molecule.

rubric.why: Hydrogen bonding raises the boiling and melting points of compounds.
rubric.description: States the effect on boiling and melting points.
rubric.how: Look for both boiling point and melting point being raised.

rubric.why: Hydrogen bonding can increase viscosity and surface tension.
rubric.description: States effects on viscosity and surface tension.
rubric.how: Look for both viscosity and surface tension being increased.

rubric.why: Hydrogen bonding reduces volatility and can affect solubility in water.
rubric.how: Look for reduced volatility or an effect on water solubility.

modelAnswer: Hydrogen bonding is the intermolecular attraction between a hydrogen atom covalently bonded to F, O, or N and an electronegative atom in a neighbouring molecule.
Hydrogen bonding holds molecules together and raises their boiling points and melting points.
It can also increase viscosity and surface tension.
It reduces volatility and affects the solubility of compounds in water.

items.followUp: Define evaporation and describe the effects of temperature, surface area and humidity on its rate.

rubric.why: Evaporation is the change of a liquid into vapour from its surface below its boiling point.
rubric.how: Look for liquid changing into vapour at the surface and below the boiling point.

rubric.why: Increasing temperature increases the rate of evaporation.
rubric.how: Look for higher temperature increasing the rate.

rubric.why: Increasing the exposed surface area increases the rate of evaporation.
rubric.description: Explains the effect of exposed surface area.
rubric.how: Look for a larger exposed surface area increasing the rate.

rubric.why: Moving air carries vapour away and increases evaporation, while higher humidity decreases it.
rubric.description: Explains the effects of air movement and humidity.
rubric.how: Look for air movement increasing evaporation and humidity decreasing it.

modelAnswer: Evaporation is the change of a liquid into vapour from its surface at a temperature below its boiling point.
Increasing the temperature increases the rate of evaporation.
Increasing the exposed surface area also increases the rate of evaporation.
Greater wind speed increases evaporation by carrying vapour away; greater humidity decreases it.
The nature of the liquid also affects its rate of evaporation: more volatile liquids evaporate faster.

items.followUp: Give four characteristics of a colloidal solution.

rubric.why: A suspension is a heterogeneous mixture.
rubric.description: Identifies the nature of a suspension.
rubric.how: Look for the term heterogeneous mixture.

rubric.why: Suspended particles are relatively large and can be seen.
rubric.description: Describes the size or visibility of suspension particles.
rubric.how: Look for particles described as large or visible.

rubric.why: Suspended particles settle when the mixture is left standing.
rubric.description: States that particles settle on standing.
rubric.how: Look for particles settling when left undisturbed.

rubric.why: Suspension particles can be separated from the liquid by filtration.
rubric.description: Gives a method of separating suspension particles.
rubric.how: Look for separation by filtration or use of a filter.

modelAnswer: A suspension is a heterogeneous mixture.
Its particles are large enough to be visible.
The particles settle down when the suspension is left standing.
The particles can be separated from the liquid by filtration.
